description: Properties of existing routing and medical foundation-model benchmarks, each verified from the benchmark's own paper (full text read 2026-11-16). Used for the main-paper comparison table (tab:bench).

columns.per_sample: outcome of every candidate on every sample, usable as a per-sample routing target
columns.collections: routing targets are sets of models fused per sample
columns.cost: price = API/token price, time = measured inference time or throughput, no = none recorded
columns.external_shift: evaluation on external cohorts or under acquisition/site shift
columns.released: per-sample model outputs released as data

rows.name: RouterBench
rows.evidence: arXiv 2403.12031 §4.3: '405,467 samples ... 11 models, 8 datasets, and 64 tasks'; App. A.3: each row holds sample id, model, response, performance, cost (API price; open models priced via Together AI); cascade returns one model's output (§5.2); 'code and data are available at github.com/withmartian/routerbench'

rows.name: RouterEval
rows.evidence: arXiv 2503.10657 / Findings EMNLP 2025: router 'is essentially an m-way classifier' over a selection vector (§4.1); 'without considering factors such as computational cost' (§2); 'we open-source over 200,000,000 performance records' (§4.3); 8,576 LLMs over 12 benchmarks (Table 4)

rows.name: RouterArena
rows.evidence: arXiv 2510.00202: 8,400 queries from 23 source datasets; 'Each query is answered by 42 LLMs' (Fig. 4) used for difficulty labels, routers scored on their own pools (partial); framework 'returns its model selections' (§5); cost from official API pricing (§4); robustness only to query perturbations; release of per-model outputs not stated

rows.name: VL-RouterBench
rows.evidence: CVPR 2026 (vlr.pdf): '14 datasets across 3 task groups, totaling 30,540 samples, and includes 15 open-source models and 2 API models, yielding 519,180 sample-model pairs'; correctness label per sample-model pair, cost from public price sheets (Eq. 3); router selects one model (Eq. 1); groups General, STEM, Charts/OCR; 'We open-source the complete data construction and evaluation toolchain' (release of the logs themselves not stated: partial)

rows.name: Campanella et al.
rows.evidence: Nat Commun 16:3640 (2025): '22 clinically relevant slide-level tasks'; 11 models named (tRes50, CTransPath, UNI, Virchow, Prov-GigaPath, SP22M, SP85M, Virchow2, h-optimus-0, Phikon-v2, Phikon); within-cohort MCCV; GPU memory and throughput on one H100 (Supp. Tables 8-9); 'Digital pathology benchmark data will not be made available'

rows.name: Neidlinger et al.
rows.evidence: Nat Biomed Eng (2025), doi 10.1038/s41551-025-01516-3: '19 foundation models and 31 clinically relevant evaluation tasks', 13 cohorts, trained on TCGA and tested on external cohorts; 14 fixed task-level ensembles (not per sample); only GPUs named, no cost; code and source data released, not per-slide predictions

rows.name: Woerner \& Baumgartner
rows.evidence: arXiv 2408.08058: 'we evaluate 16 publicly available models'; MedIMeta 'comprised of 19 different datasets from 10 different imaging modalities'; code only

rows.name: Nguyen et al.
rows.evidence: arXiv 2607.10358: 'We evaluate 15 foundation-model backbones under a unified frozen-backbone source-to-external ID/OOD protocol across these three tasks' (density, BI-RADS, cancer); 15 datasets from 12 countries/regions; code only

ours.name: HealthRouter-Bench
ours.evidence: router_main.json (10 candidates, 4 tasks, measured candidate_cost_ms), router_external.json (4 cohorts x 5 conditions), router_general.json (EuroSAT, DTD); CVPR27_release/healthrouter/MANIFEST.md: per-image outputs released for PatchCamelyon, CBIS-DDSM, EuroSAT, Camelyon17-WILDS, IDRiD, CMMD (6 of 10 sources); Shenzhen, Montgomery, APTOS, DTD not released (no licence permitting it)
